title: The wave-pinning crawler regrows its lost size after a front cut only if its polarity protein is made at a fixed rate per cell: per-cell synthesis restores the twin's area and speed within 6-16 t (2 seeds), while synthesis per unit area leaves size neutral and the cut cell keeps shrinking
summary: The crawler audit (20261025T2114-c23-audit-wavepin) showed that a front-cut cell re-forms its front but stays at 66% of its twin's area, because its protein total is conserved. world.py imports the claimed crawler unchanged and adds protein turnover: both protein forms decay at kdeg, and synthesis goes into the cytosol. Per-area synthesis (ksyn = 0.46, kdeg = 0.2, so the protein total relaxes to 2.3 x area, which matches the intact cell's 6.0 at area 2.62): the twin holds area 2.61-2.66 and protein 6.0, but the cut cell (30% front sector at t=8, 27% area and 32% protein lost) keeps losing both, from 1.89/4.09 to 1.59/3.78 by t=24. At faster turnover (kdeg 0.5) it goes from 1.85/4.02 to 1.26/3.06 and is still falling. Protein per area is pinned but the size is not, and the small cell drifts down. Per-cell synthesis (kdeg x Ncell per cell, spread over its area, Ncell = 6, so the protein total relaxes to 6): the cut cell re-forms one front, and its protein and area climb back to the twin's. Seed 5 (kdeg 0.2): area 1.90 -> 2.58, protein 4.12 -> 5.92 by t=24. Seed 6 (kdeg 0.5): area 1.90 -> 2.60 by t=16, protein 6.00. It then crawls at the twin's speed (0.418 vs 0.422, 0.423 vs 0.424). Full repair, front and size, therefore needs a per-cell protein set-point. This is homeostasis imposed through the source term, so the regrowth holds by construction; the front competition that restores polarity is the crawler's own.

finding.operator: polarity-protein turnover in the wave-pinning crawler: per-cell synthesis (fixed protein set-point) vs per-area synthesis
finding.control: branched undamaged twins in every run; per-area synthesis (same turnover rates) as the matched alternative; conserved-protein crawler (audit) as the baseline
finding.result: area of the cut cell at the end vs twin: per-cell 2.58 vs 2.61 (s5, kdeg 0.2, t=24) and 2.59 vs 2.60 (s6, kdeg 0.5); per-area 1.59 vs 2.66 and 1.26 vs 2.51 (s5, still falling); conserved protein (audit) 1.73 vs 2.62

limits: One cell per run; the per-cell rule uses the whole-domain cell area and is undefined for dividing cells. The set-point Ncell is imposed, so size regrowth is by construction; only the polarity recovery is emergent. Two seeds for per-cell and one for per-area; synthesis is not yet tied to a consumed resource (the world has a resource switch, res=1, which is untested).
